History of the Semicolon

Origins

The semicolon was invented in 1494 by the Venetian printer Aldus Manutius, who used it to separate words of opposed meaning and to indicate interdependent statements.

Earlier Greek and Latin writing used dots and spacing to mark pauses, but the modern punctuation mark took shape in the Renaissance print shop.

Adoption

English writers adopted the semicolon unevenly; it became common in the eighteenth century and has been debated by stylists ever since.

Some authors avoid it entirely while others treat it as the mark of a well-built sentence.
